text: I see you are experiencing yellowing of the skin and eyes along with agitation. To help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any darkening of your urine or pale, clay-colored stools recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior, I need to rule out viral hepatitis; have you experienced any recent abdominal pain, nausea, or unexplained weight loss? REQUEST TEST: Liver Function Tests

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significantly reduced synthetic function and history of high-risk behavior, we must urgently differentiate between viral and toxic causes. Have you consumed any wild mushrooms, used acetaminophen recently, or had any known contact with individuals who have hepatitis? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis Serology Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Since viral hepatitis is ruled out, I need to assess for other toxic or metabolic causes. Have you taken any over-the-counter pain relievers like acetaminophen, or are you experiencing any abdominal pain or fever? REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal acetaminophen levels and negative hepatitis serology, I suspect acute liver failure secondary to recreational drug toxicity or Wilson's disease. REQUEST TEST: Ceruloplasmin and Urine Copper Levels

speaker: Doctor
text: With viral, acetaminophen, and Wilson's disease ruled out, I suspect acute liver failure due to a recreational drug or herbal supplement. Have you ingested any new supplements, powders, or unknown substances in the last few weeks? REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Toxicology Screen

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal toxicology screen and negative workup for common causes, I need to evaluate for autoimmune or vascular etiologies. Do you have any history of autoimmune diseases, and have you noticed any abdominal swelling or tenderness? REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune Hepatitis Panel and Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: With common causes ruled out, I suspect a metabolic disorder like Wilson's disease despite normal ceruloplasmin, or perhaps acute Budd-Chiari syndrome. Have you noticed any abdominal pain or swelling, and do you have a history of bleeding disorders or recent long periods of immobility? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Doppler Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: With all common and secondary causes ruled out, I must consider an acute viral infection that may not have shown up on the initial standard panel, such as Hepatitis E or a rare variant. Do you recall any recent travel to endemic areas or consumption of undercooked shellfish or pork? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis E IgM and Hepatitis A IgM

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute liver failure secondary to recreational drug toxicity (likely due to a novel psychoactive substance or adulterant not detected on standard toxicology screens)
